authorityBoundary.classification: Operator bearer-protected local catalog and draft persistence; not passive or external discovery.
authorityBoundary.positive: Name-only discovery performs no provider/docs/network call. Unknown exchanges become BLOCKED review drafts with liveExecutionEnabled false and withdrawal/transfer forbidden; the bounded routes never accept secrets or invoke connector/trade activation.
authorityBoundary.separation: Connector credentials, permission proof and trade admission remain separate KAIROS control families and cannot inherit registry status.

criticalFindings.finding: The UI promises a support check, but discover only compares four hard-coded records/aliases or registers arbitrary text. Official URLs and Rapira notes have no retrieval, source digest, owner, version, as-of, license, region, jurisdiction or independent verification.
A builtin CCXT name is immediately labelled READ_ONLY while public/private/balance tests remain not_run and no installed-version, API, credential or permission proof occurred.

The unreachable legacy body behind /api/exchanges/test's unconditional 409 would mark registry READY and claim read_trade_key_present plus fee/min/precision capabilities after load_markets and fetch_balance only. If re-enabled it would overstate spot-submit/readback, withdrawal/transfer denial and complete capability proof. Registry status is not engine admission.

Registry persistence has no lock, CAS, fsync, schema validation, writer audit or revision ledger. Parse errors become an empty registry and startup reseeding can overwrite the recoverable view; draft writes overwrite directly without history or digest.

ExchangeDiscoverIn has no length/pattern bound; lossy 64-character slugging creates collisions. The build route auto-registers missing IDs and can overwrite a builtin CCXT record to draft/BLOCKED, while old fields override refreshed builtin metadata.

No immutable request/idempotency/correlation ID, reviewer/four-eyes approval, revision, rejection/revocation, expiry, retention, rollback or recovery event exists; rebuild overwrites the same artifact.
Builder responses expose the absolute local draft path rather than a content-addressed artifact ID.
Operator chat and dormant engine chat duplicate registry/builder writes, increasing semantic and recovery drift; the SPA has no caller for detail/build review lifecycle.

telegramBot.reason: No customer/bot exchange-adapter discovery exists; KAIROS operator chat is a separate control surface.

site.reason: Customer site must not register or approve CEX adapters.

miniApp.reason: Mini App has no adapter discovery authority and must not gain it.

admin.reason: KAIROS SPA lists/registers candidates, but provenance, scoped approval and recovery are unaccepted.

api.reason: Bearer-protected list/discover/detail/build routes persist metadata and drafts without an accepted lifecycle.

native.reason: Native wallet must never become exchange-adapter onboarding authority.

limitations: No authenticated API, provider/docs/network, customer row, secret value, registry/draft writer, connector, trade, deploy or restart was exercised.
No egress in the four bounded registry routes is a source observation, not proof that adjacent chat, configurable AI or dormant connector paths are safe.

The 25 currently enumerated families are classified and the bounded omissions list is empty. No post-expansion closure rescan of the full deployed/generated route, startup/import-writer, worker/service and UI/bot-consumer universe was performed; this does not prove that no material family is omitted and does not accept E0.4.
